title: Teachers and AI: Understanding the factors influencing AI integration in K-12 education
extended_summary:
This paper examines the psychological and pedagogical factors that shape K-12 teachers’ readiness to integrate generative AI into instructional practice. The authors focus on why teachers embrace or resist AI, including perceived usefulness, student engagement, curriculum alignment, cultural fit, ethical concerns, technical barriers, and workload. The study is positioned as a response to the growing interest in AI in education and the need to understand teachers’ roles in successful implementation.

The empirical work was conducted in a 14-week professional development course at a private school in Türkiye. Sixty-six teachers from 11 disciplines participated, with representation across pre-school, primary school, and high school. Participants engaged with generative AI tools such as ChatGPT, MagicSchool, Canva, Gamma, and Character.ai through online discussion forums and an AI-supported learning activity design task. Their reflections and designed activities were analyzed using inductive thematic analysis.

Findings suggest that teachers valued AI for efficiency, adaptability, interactive learning, and support for lesson planning and differentiation. At the same time, they reported barriers related to technical problems, device access, time demands, curriculum mismatch, language and cultural issues, and ethical concerns such as privacy, fairness, plagiarism, and reduced student creativity. The paper concludes that effective AI integration in K-12 education requires targeted teacher support, infrastructure, ethical guidance, and better alignment between AI tools and local curricular and cultural contexts.

identified_tools.name: ChatGPT
identified_tools.description: OpenAI's generative AI chatbot based on GPT models, used for dialogue, content generation, and instructional support.
identified_tools.use_case: Used by teachers in a professional development course and in designed classroom activities for lesson planning, generating instructional content, creating questions, summaries, stories, presentations, and feedback/improvement tasks.

findings.finding_summary: In this qualitative study of 66 teachers from a private school in Türkiye, ChatGPT was the most commonly used AI tool in the 59 analyzed designed activities. Teachers reported it supported lesson planning, content creation, differentiated instruction, story/dictation generation, and feedback-oriented tasks, but also noted curriculum misalignment, language, and cultural limitations.
findings.measure: Teacher-reported tool use and thematic analysis of designed learning activities and forum reflections

identified_tools.name: MagicSchool
identified_tools.description: An AI-powered teacher tool platform offering multiple utilities for lesson planning, content creation, student support, and related classroom tasks.
identified_tools.use_case: Used and discussed by K-12 teachers as a lesson-planning and instructional support tool during AI-focused professional development and activity design.

findings.finding_summary: In this qualitative study of 66 teachers, MagicSchool was among the most valued tools after ChatGPT. Teachers highlighted its variety of tools, usefulness for adapting materials to lessons, and support for planning, differentiation, progress tracking, and performance evaluation, while also noting broader implementation barriers such as alignment and workload.
findings.measure: Teacher-reported preferences, reflections, and thematic analysis of designed activities

identified_tools.name: Canva
identified_tools.description: A digital design platform with AI-enabled features for creating visual content, presentations, and educational materials.
identified_tools.use_case: Mentioned by teachers as one of the AI tools used in designed activities and as a preferred tool for visual and interactive learning materials.

findings.finding_summary: Teachers included Canva among the preferred tools in their designed activities and associated it with visual design, animated characters, and interactive story/presentation creation. The paper does not report quantitative effects, but the qualitative findings indicate teachers viewed it as useful for visual and differentiated instruction.
findings.measure: Teacher-reported preferences and thematic analysis of designed activities

identified_tools.name: Gamma
identified_tools.description: An AI-assisted presentation/content creation tool used for generating slide decks and visual materials.
identified_tools.use_case: Used by teachers for generating presentations in designed activities and discussed as a tool that made work easier.

findings.finding_summary: Teachers reported Gamma as helpful for quickly preparing presentation files and supporting presentation-related classroom activities. The study provides qualitative evidence of perceived efficiency and ease of use rather than quantitative impact.

identified_tools.name: Character.ai
identified_tools.description: A chatbot platform that allows users to create and interact with character-based conversational agents.
identified_tools.use_case: Used in teachers' designed activities for discussions, role-play, and creative learning tasks.

findings.finding_summary: Teachers used Character.ai in designed activities for character creation, discussion, and reflective tasks. In the qualitative analysis, it was associated with constructivist, critical-thinking, and creative-expression strategies, but no quantitative effect was reported.

quality_tier_rationale: This is an exploratory qualitative study with 66 teachers from a single private school and no experimental comparison group. It provides rich descriptive evidence but not causal impact estimates.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper reports strong perceived usefulness across several tools, but it does not provide effect sizes or outcome metrics. Impact is therefore suggestive rather than measurable from the reported data.
